text: [thoughtful] Now suppose the browser tabs and the rest of the desktop are also hard to see. [short pause] Page zoom will not solve every part of that problem. [short pause] System text size changes text in supported areas; display scaling changes the size of text, apps, and other interface elements more broadly. [short pause] The exact controls depend on your computer. [short pause] Ask the instructor before changing a shared workstation's system settings. [short pause] This is like choosing between a magnifying glass for one page and a more comfortable arrangement for the whole desk. [short pause] [curious] Which would you try first if only one website is too small? [short pause] [confident] Browser zoom, because it matches the scope of the problem.

text: [warmly] Picture a radio connected to headphones. [short pause] Turning up the radio does not make the room speaker play if the sound is still going to the headphones. [short pause] [interested] A computer can work the same way. [short pause] First check whether the sound is muted. [short pause] Then inspect the selected output device: speakers, a monitor, or a headset. [short pause] Choose the device you intend to hear, begin at a comfortable volume, and play a short test. [short pause] If that test works but a meeting does not, check the meeting app's own audio choice next. [short pause] [encouraging] Change one setting at a time. [short pause] This gives you evidence about what fixed the problem instead of leaving you with several unexplained changes.

text: [interested] Start with the words that describe your task, the kind of service, and the location. [short pause] Computer help library plus your town is more useful than typing help by itself. [short pause] [reassuring] If there are no useful results, remove one restriction rather than assuming the service does not exist. [short pause] Filters can help, but they can also hide a relevant page. [short pause] [encouraging] [short pause] Pause and write a search for your chosen community task.
